name: What to Prepare Before You Start Cabinet Refacing

step.name: Step 1: Empty Your Cabinets Completely: This might seem obvious, but it’s c…
step.text: Empty Your Cabinets Completely: This might seem obvious, but it’s crucial. All contents, from dishes to pots and pans, need to be removed from your cabinets. Think of it as an opportunity to declutter and organize! Store these items in another room or in labeled boxes that won’t be in the way during installation. This makes it easier for our team to access the cabinet boxes and saves you time during the project.

step.name: Step 2: Clear Your Countertops: Just like your cabinets, your countertops n…
step.text: Clear Your Countertops: Just like your cabinets, your countertops need to be completely clear of appliances, décor, and anything else. This ensures our team has ample space to work, measure, and apply new materials without obstructions. It also protects your items from dust and accidental damage.

step.name: Step 3: Think About Your Design Vision: Before we start, have a good idea o…
step.text: Think About Your Design Vision: Before we start, have a good idea of the aesthetic you're aiming for. This includes considering door styles, finishes (like a new wood veneer or laminate), and potential hardware choices. Gathering inspiration photos or creating a mood board can really help communicate your vision, ensuring the final result truly reflects your style. Our design team can help you with CAD-supported layouts to visualize the possibilities.

step.name: Step 4: Confirm Structural Soundness: While we'll do our own thorough inspe…
step.text: Confirm Structural Soundness: While we'll do our own thorough inspection, it's helpful for you to be aware of any areas where your existing cabinet boxes might feel weak, warped, or show signs of moisture. Refacing relies on a sturdy foundation, so addressing any underlying issues beforehand is key to a lasting finish. If there are major structural concerns, we'll discuss the best approach.

step.name: Step 5: Review the Project Schedule: We believe in clear communication and…
step.text: Review the Project Schedule: We believe in clear communication and transparency. Understanding the anticipated timeline, from material ordering to on-site installation, helps you plan your daily routines. Material selection and ordering usually take 1–3 weeks for stock items or 2–4 weeks for custom, with on-site installation often taking 2–5 working days.
